title: Integrating network pharmacology and in vivo pharmacological validation to explore the gastroprotective mechanism of Sotetsuflavone against indomethacin-induced gastric ulcer in rats: Involvement of JAK2/STAT3 pathway.
authors: Tabaa, Manar M El; Harty, Mohammed E El; Mohsen, Mohamed; Rashad, Eman; Negm, Walaa A; Elmorshedy, Kadreya; Abu-Risha, Sally E
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄酮化合物Sotetsuflavone对吲哚美辛诱导胃溃疡的保护机制，涉及JAK2/STAT3通路和分子对接，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或MD方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Sotetsuflavone (SF) is an antioxidant flavonoid derived from the Cycas thouarsii R.Br. plant. Although SF regulates numerous cellular pathways influencing inflammation, its antiinflammatory benefits against gastric ulcers are less well-studied. Hence, it is imperative to thoroughly understand the potential gastroprotective mechanisms of SF. This study aimed to explore the effectiveness of SF against indomethacin (IND)-induced gastric ulcers. Network analysis and molecular docking were used to identify the specific targets and pathways related to SF and stomach ulcers. To validate the in vivo pharmacological action of SF, 36 rats were divided into six groups. Ulcer index (UI), protective percentage (PP), gastric mucosal mediators, oxidant/antioxidant status, and inflammatory markers (MIF, M-CSF, and AIF-1) were assessed. Additionally, the expression of PI3K, Akt, Siah2, SOCS3, JAK2, and STAT3 was determined. Stomach histopathology and immunohistochemistry were done. Network pharmacology detected 46 overlapping targets between SF and stomach ulcers, with HIF1A as the primary target among the top hubs. The network also revealed that JAK/STAT, PI3K/Akt, and HIF-1A signaling are among the top 50 markedly enriched KEGG pathways. Furthermore, docking results confirmed that SF has a strong binding affinity towards SOCS3, JAK2, STAT3, M-CSF (CSF-1), and AIF-1. Therefore, we hypothesized that the JAK2/STAT3 pathway may be primarily responsible for SF antiinflammatory action. Through up-regulating SOCS3, SF altered the PI3K/Akt pathway, mitigating oxidative stress, blocking the outflow of inflammatory mediators, and impeding gastric ulcer development. Overall, SF, by the SOCS3-mediated JAK2/STAT3 suppression, might considerably reduce oxidative stress, inflammation, and ulceration caused by indomethacin in the stomach.
abstract_zh: Sotetsuflavone (SF) 是一种源自苏铁（Cycas thouarsii R.Br.）植物的抗氧化黄酮类化合物。尽管SF调节多种影响炎症的细胞通路，但其对胃溃疡的抗炎益处研究较少。因此，深入理解SF潜在的胃保护机制至关重要。本研究旨在探讨SF对吲哚美辛（IND）诱导胃溃疡的有效性。采用网络分析和分子对接（molecular docking）来识别与SF和胃溃疡相关的特定靶点及通路。为验证SF的体内药理作用，将36只大鼠分为六组。评估了溃疡指数（UI）、保护百分比（PP）、胃黏膜介质、氧化/抗氧化状态及炎症标志物（MIF、M-CSF和AIF-1）。此外，测定了PI3K、Akt、Siah2、SOCS3、JAK2和STAT3的表达。进行了胃组织病理学和免疫组织化学检查。网络药理学检测到SF与胃溃疡之间的46个重叠靶点，其中HIF1A是主要枢纽中的首要靶点。网络还揭示，JAK/STAT、PI3K/Akt和HIF-1A信号通路位列前50个显著富集的KEGG通路中。此外，对接结果确认SF对SOCS3、JAK2、STAT3、M-CSF（CSF-1）和AIF-1具有强结合亲和力。因此，我们假设JAK2/STAT3通路可能主要负责SF的抗炎作用。通过上调SOCS3，SF改变了PI3K/Akt通路，减轻氧化应激，阻断炎症介质外流，并阻碍胃溃疡发展。总体而言，SF通过SOCS3介导的JAK2/STAT3抑制，可能显著减少吲哚美辛引起的胃部氧化应激、炎症和溃疡形成。
